query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Optimizing the nozzle-to-substrate (spray) distance in the HVAF-i7 process to a range of 300–350 mm will boost particle velocity, thereby increasing deposition efficiency and yielding a thicker, adherent FeCoNiCrAl bond coat with minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy powder with a 15–45 μm feedstock distribution.
generation.intervention: Set the HVAF-i7 spray distance to 300–350 mm.
generation.conditions: Deposition under high-temperature oxidation–resistant bond coat conditions applicable to substrates with internal diameters as small as 120 mm and under thermal-barrier service service requirements.
generation.structural_mediator: Increased particle kinetic energy that improves in-flight dynamics, splat formation, and inter-particle bonding.
generation.mechanism: Reducing the spray distance to 300–350 mm increases particle velocity at impact, which enhances flattening and bonding of the particles, leading to an improved deposition efficiency and thicker build-up while keeping in-flight oxidation low.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline HVAF-i7 process using standard spray distances, the optimized setup is expected to produce a significantly thicker and adherent bond coat with maintained minimal oxidation.
generation.baseline: Coating deposition using standard HVAF-i7 parameters with 15–45 μm feedstock, which yields acceptable quality but insufficient coating thickness.
generation.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective for the current torch/nozzle configuration and under the typical processing atmospheres used for high-temperature thermal-barrier applications within confined geometries (down to 120 mm internal diameters).
generation.uncertainty: There is moderate uncertainty regarding the precise tuning of spray distance for different torch setups and potential trade-offs if excessively short distances are used.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a controlled experiment depositing FeCoNiCrAl bond coats using the HVAF-i7 torch with two settings: the current standard spray distance and an optimized 300–350 mm spray distance. All other parameters (feedstock size, composition, substrate conditions) must be kept constant.
measurements: Oxidation levels (via surface analysis techniques such as XPS or EDS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coatings deposited at the optimized spray distance (300–350 mm) do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in thickness with maintained adhesion and low oxidation levels compared to those produced at the standard distance, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: Reducing the HVAF-i7 spray distance to increase particle velocity will improve deposition efficiency and yield a thicker, adherent FeCoNiCrAl bond coat without compromising coating quality.
drafts.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock with a particle size range of 15–45 μm prepared for HVAF-i7 deposition.
drafts.intervention: Decrease the spray distance during HVAF-i7 processing to attain higher particle kinetic energy on impact, similar to the nozzle-specific best spray distances (300–350 mm) reported for the HVAF-M3 system.
drafts.conditions: Deposition using the HVAF-i7 torch under typical processing settings for internal diameters as small as 120 mm, ensuring minimal as-sprayed oxidation and maintained coating integrity during high-temperature thermal barrier service.
drafts.structural_mediator: Enhanced particle impact energy leading to improved flattening, bonding, and build-up of the coating layers.
drafts.mechanism: A reduced spray distance increases the velocity (and hence kinetic energy) of the feedstock particles at impact. This enhanced energy facilitates greater particle deformation and interfacial bonding, resulting in a thicker coat while keeping oxidation low by reducing in-flight exposure time.
drafts.predicted_outcome: An HVAF-i7 coating produced at the reduced spray distance will display a significantly increased thickness relative to the baseline (15–45 μm feedstock at standard distance), while still possessing the desired adhesion, minimal oxidation, and durability under high-temperature conditions.
drafts.baseline: Coatings produced with the existing HVAF-i7 process using 15–45 μm feedstock that show acceptable quality but insufficient thickness.
drafts.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective when the shortened spray distance does not overly expose the feedstock to excessive heat or oxidation risks. Its success may be limited to the current torch/nozzle configuration and similar processing atmospheres; excessively short spray distances might deteriorate coating properties.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a series of HVAF-i7 depositions using the same 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock while systematically varying the spray distance (for example, testing distances at 250, 300, 350, and 400 mm). Maintain all other deposition parameters constant. Evaluate the resulting coatings for thickness, adhesion, and oxidation levels.
measurements: Coating thickness via cross-sectional optical or electron microscopy
Adhesion strength through standardized pull-off tests
Oxidation content using surface analysis methods (e.g., XPS or EDS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If reducing the spray distance does not yield a statistically significant increase in coating thickness—without causing unacceptable increases in oxidation or loss of adhesion—when compared to the baseline HVAF-i7 process, then the intervention fails to support the hypothesis.
